about: PerfR9 (plan R9 and the 50 ms daily step), 2026-10-15, seed 1, AMD RDNA-1, headless Chrome 150 at 1600x1000, default warm, 12 s each. 'r9' is this build (mask after the world tested against a ground-only depth, cull rounds placing each workgroup's sprites, specks and rows with one atomic a list, clasts including pebbles drawn from per-cell GPU caches); 'base' is 09a2904 built and served beside it and run straight after. The machine was at load 7 to 36 with peers' Bun/Dawn GPU jobs holding up to 3.7 GB of the 4 GB of VRAM, so the same build swung by 2x between runs (base orbit 18.02 then 10.07 then 10.42 ms mean): the figures are not comparable with bench-sim-worker.json, which was taken on a quieter machine, and R9 is not shown here either way.

dailyStep.note: src/gpu stems' law plus the deadwood's day, per-kernel GPU timestamps on a store holding seed 1's flora and deadwood (scratch profiler, day 3). The stick bins' sweep took 48.8 ms of it because a day's tenth of the bins ran every invocation (one live lane in ten); it now runs one invocation a bin of the day's share and stops at the first stick still lying (kill mode reads no count): 0.1 ms. Coefficients are worked out ahead over the day's hours (stemDriver.ahead, uploaded as made), so the law's CPU part fell from 20 to 54 ms to 3.7 to 8 ms. The landing no longer unpacks 10 million heights: the pack lists the generator's stems that died and the heights are kept as a view of the landed copy (flora land 33 ms to 0.1 to 1 ms).
dailyStep.gap: The raster's count and file kernels stay at 8 to 10 ms each in place against under 1 ms in isolation (first-touch and clock ramp after the idle hours, under the peers' VRAM pressure); the wall day (begin plus GPU) measured 59 to 98 ms on this loaded machine, so the 50 ms budget is not shown.

r9.note: run first, under load (sun and shade, unchanged, cost 1.6 and 1.4x the quiet run's); pebbles now drawn (7,866 specks at the close view)

benches.missing: turn and pan, the zoom of the final build and scripts/play/objects.ts were not run before the run's budget ran out
